newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down on late soymeal losses.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down on late soymeal losses.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower Thursday in response to a late sell-off in soybean meal and continued good prospects for South American oilseed crops, CBOT traders said.
"Rosenthal started selling the meal, that's what brought everything down," a floor trader said.
Volume on the day was estimated to be very light following the Christmas holiday on Wednesday, so losses were somewhat exaggerated, floor sources said.
Recent reports from Argentina and Brazil have showed those crop prospects remained favorable because of good weather.
The possibility that both those nations will produce huge soybean crops is expected to continue to weigh on CBOT prices and limit gains, traders said.

Earlier in the session, soybeans traded higher on strength provided by a strong close on Tuesday, traders said. Other supportive factors included slow farmer sales in the U.S. and continued active exports, traders said.
January soybeans settled down 5-1/4 cents per bushel at $7.01-3/4, and March closed down 6-3/4 at $6.96-1/2.
Refco Inc sold three million bushels of January, Prudential Securities sold two million March. Iowa Grain bought 1.5 million bushels March, floor sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 30,000 contracts, above the 22,758 contracts traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In options trading, Cargill Investor Services sold 300 July $8.00 calls and Farmers Commodity Corp bought 360 March $7.25 calls and sold 90 July $7.00 puts, floor sources said.
